alt: The memo array filling in as the top-down recursion returns. A cell starts empty; the first time its stair is needed, the recursion computes it and stores the result; every later call for that same stair looks the stored value up instead of recomputing it.

steps.caption: `ways(4)` is computed for the first time and stored: `memo[4] = 2`.
`ways(3)` is computed for the first time and stored: `memo[3] = 3`.
`ways(4)` is needed again. `memo[4]` already holds 2, so it is looked up instead of recomputed.
`ways(2)` is computed for the first time and stored: `memo[2] = 5`.
`ways(3)` is needed again. `memo[3]` already holds 3, so it is looked up instead of recomputed.
`ways(1)` is computed for the first time and stored: `memo[1] = 8`.
`ways(2)` is needed again. `memo[2]` already holds 5, so it is looked up instead of recomputed.
`ways(0)` is computed for the first time and stored: `memo[0] = 13`.
`ways(1)` is computed for the first time and stored: `memo[1] = 2`.
`ways(0)` is computed for the first time and stored: `memo[0] = 3`.
